comments.body:
Collision analysis (paused pending coordination).

This BUG (c6bd-b10e-74f1-407f) and lemuroid-compliant-hoopoe (39a2-4832-e436-4850, in_progress, actively worked by a sibling agent) describe the SAME root cause and SAME fix, and hoopoe has declared file_impact on the IDENTICAL files.

Confirmed mechanism (matches the recorded RCA): resolve_ref() in src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py (~L262-266) calls fetch_origin() with no target ref before rev_parse, which becomes 'git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin' in git_fetch.fetch_origin (~L256-283). On a checkout whose remote.origin.fetch maps every head, git transfers all origin heads (incl. the large tickets branch) even when only a locally-present code SHA is needed -> 300s timeout, zero model calls.

Fix location is a single shared seam (resolve_ref/fetch_origin) that hoopoe already owns via declared file_impact:
- src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py
- src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py
- new test tests/unit/test_snapshot_targeted_fetch.py

Confirmed the general fetch here is ONLY for ref freshness/resolution: blob acquisition for the selected tree is handled separately by _ensure_blobs_present() (targeted 'git fetch --no-filter --refetch <sha>'), so skipping the general fetch for a present full SHA preserves complete blob materialization. Proposed minimal fix: in resolve_ref, when ref is a full 40-hex SHA that rev_parse resolves locally, return it WITHOUT any general fetch; moving branches/tags still fetch; an absent SHA still uses the existing targeted-fetch fallback.

Because hoopoe is actively editing the same two functions, implementing here independently would collide on the same lines and duplicate the work. I have messaged the hoopoe agent to coordinate ownership (absorb fossa as duplicate, vs. I take a non-overlapping slice: the present-full-SHA regression test + docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md fetch-scope update layered on hoopoe's change). Holding all code edits until hoopoe replies.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Duplicate determination — runtime-confirmed, linked duplicates->lemuroid-compliant-hoopoe (39a2-4832-e436-4850).

RUNTIME REPRODUCTION (deterministic local remote): a fresh clone with the default broad refspec (+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*) and an unrelated large 'tickets' branch. With the target commit already present locally (full 40-hex SHA c2b79f4b...), resolve_ref(sha, clone, fetch=True, blobless=False) still issued exactly:
  git -C <clone> -c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=10 fetch --quiet --no-filter origin
i.e. a broad no-filter fetch whose scope expands through remote.origin.fetch to every head — no target ref passed — even though rev_parse resolves the SHA with zero network. This is the recorded mechanism (repo_snapshot.resolve_ref ~L262-266 -> git_fetch.fetch_origin ~L256-283) confirmed empirically.

WHY DUPLICATE (not merely related): lemuroid-compliant-hoopoe has the same title/root cause (attested ref materialization broad-fetches all origin heads), declared file_impact on the IDENTICAL seam (src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py, src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py, tests/unit/test_snapshot_targeted_fetch.py), and its ACs subsume this ticket's. hoopoe's own Context section cites the SAME 512.139s run (from unromantic-ferny-arawana) that this ticket's Proof section cites. The fixes would edit the same function bodies with the same intent; a second competing Gerrit change would be redundant.

SHARED CODE PATH FOR THE REVIEWER: the correct fix lives in resolve_ref — skip the general fetch_origin() when ref is a full 40-hex SHA that rev_parse resolves locally (return it directly); keep the general fetch for moving branches/tags; keep the existing targeted-fetch fallback for an absent SHA. Blob acquisition is UNAFFECTED because it is handled separately by _ensure_blobs_present() (targeted 'git fetch --no-filter --refetch <sha>'), so a present-SHA short-circuit still materializes all blobs.

DISPOSITION: not opening a competing change. hoopoe owns the code fix; this ticket is left claimed for coordinator/human disposition (recommend closing as duplicate once hoopoe's change lands and satisfies the shared acceptance criteria). If hoopoe stalls, this ticket can be reopened for independent implementation using the minimal fix above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
UPDATE — not a pure duplicate; implementing the follow-on fix. The hoopoe agent confirmed (via coordination) that lemuroid-compliant-hoopoe change 2178 (merged as origin/main 60348ef146fa) SCOPES resolve_ref's opening fetch to the requested ref but does NOT short-circuit it: for a bare full SHA it still issues a targeted single-object 'git fetch ... <sha>' want. My distinguishing acceptance criterion — a locally-present full SHA must trigger NO fetch at all — is therefore genuinely uncovered. Retagged our link duplicates -> relates_to.

PROVEN RCA (runtime, /rebar-debug Phase 1):
- Root cause lineage: attested resolution has fetched-before-resolve unconditionally since the snapshot materialization core (story hoot-glove-foyer, 6d56-8c12-9953-4d25). Originally that opening fetch was an unscoped 'git fetch --no-filter origin' that expanded through remote.origin.fetch to every head (the 512s/300s-timeout field failure). lemuroid-compliant-hoopoe narrowed the blast radius by scoping the refspec, but left a residual: an immutable full SHA already present locally still pays a network round-trip (a scoped want) it does not owe.
- Confirmed mechanism: with hoopoe's merged code, resolve_ref -> fetch_origin(ref=scoped_fetch_target(sha)) = the sha verbatim as a targeted want. On a --filter=blob:none clone (all commits/trees present), the commit object is already local, so rev_parse resolves it with zero network; the want is pure latency and, on a wedged remote, a needless failure path.
- Falsifiable RED test proves it: tests/unit/test_snapshot_present_sha_no_fetch.py::test_present_full_sha_issues_no_fetch spies git-fetch argv; pre-fix it records the targeted want (RED), post-fix it records ZERO fetches (GREEN). Verified by reverting the guard: 1 failed (that test) / 3 passed; with the guard: 4 passed.

FIX (Phase 2, minimal, layered on hoopoe's merge):
- New predicate git_fetch.is_present_full_sha(repo_root, ref): True only for a FULL 40/64-hex object name whose commit is already local. Presence is probed OFFLINE with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 (cat-file -e) so a promisor/partial clone does NOT lazily fetch during the check — an absent object returns non-zero and falls through to the explicit targeted-want path.
- resolve_ref gates its opening fetch: 'if remote_present and not is_present_full_sha(root, ref)'. Moving branches/tags still refresh (scoped); an absent full SHA still takes hoopoe's targeted want and fails closed; blob materialization is unaffected (_ensure_blobs_present does its own targeted --refetch of the SHA).

GUARDRAILS: repo_snapshot.py kept at exactly the 800-LOC cap (predicate lives in git_fetch.py; +1 import offset by tightening an adjacent comment). resolve_ref C901 8->9 (<15, not baselined). make lint, make typecheck, and 512 snapshot/fetch tests (security, partial-clone, timeout, concurrency, plus hoopoe's targeted-fetch tests) all green; test_snapshot_docs green after documenting fetch scope in docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md.

caused_by note: root origin is hoot-glove-foyer (unconditional fetch-before-resolve); a caused_by link there is blocked because that ticket has no trailer-bearing commit and agents must not --force, so attribution is recorded here in prose.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

An attested gate against a locally present full commit SHA still performs a general fetch before resolving the SHA. In a checkout whose `remote.origin.fetch` maps every head, this becomes `git fetch --no-filter origin`. Git applies the broad refspec and fetches every configured head, including `tickets`, although the gate will materialize one code commit.

The current snapshot contract states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the committed tree at the selected SHA. A locally present full SHA does not need remote freshness. The general fetch adds unrelated transfer cost and can prevent the gate from reaching model execution.

## Rebar-debug orientation

- Step 0(a). Searches for `promisor`, `broad-fetch performance`, `snapshot no-filter partial clone pack bloat`, and the exact timeout found related closed tickets but no bug with this scope. `suave-constant-cow` handles byte-starved transport stalls. `agrologic-oval-bobolink` handles uncoordinated ref updates. Neither limits the ref set of a successful no-filter fetch.
- Step 0(b). The occurrence was reported against `813baac9b01524a024523a8516d563b17f395358`.
- Step 0(c). The F30A worktree matched `origin/main` at that revision.

## Confirmed mechanism

`resolve_ref` calls `fetch_origin` without a target before it attempts `rev_parse`, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` lines 262 through 266. Materializing callers pass `blobless=False`. `fetch_origin` therefore constructs a general `git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin` and bounds the subprocess at 300 seconds, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py` lines 256 through 283. The configured `remote.origin.fetch` decides which heads that command transfers.

The affected checkout uses `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`. A main-only comparison checkout uses `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`. The remote currently has 19 heads. The broad checkout contains about 12 GB of Git objects, 115 packs, and recent packs ranging from about 160 MB to 338 MB. One unfinished pack is about 2.3 GB.

## Proof

- F30A completion verification against the full SHA made no model call and failed after the production 300 second fetch timeout. A direct `git fetch origin main` had completed in 3.9 seconds shortly before.
- Ticket `unromantic-ferny-arawana` records an independent run at the same revision. Its broad partial-clone checkout made zero model calls and failed after 512.139 seconds because the general fetch reached the 300 second timeout. Its main-only comparison checkout crossed the fetch boundary and completed with signed PASS in 133.411 seconds.
- The F30A isolated main-only clone also crossed this boundary and completed an attested plan review with signed PASS.
- The target commit tree contains 3,550 objects and zero missing objects in the affected checkout. Materialization did not require a general fetch to acquire this tree.
- Source inspection and process sampling rule out the enrich drain as the direct blocker. Enrich drain releases its advisory lock before model work at `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` lines 358 through 428. It does not own the code snapshot fetch lock.

The configuration differential distinguishes broad ref selection from provider latency, credentials, an absent target object, and the enrich-drain lock. Transport stalls remain possible in general, but they do not explain why the main-only comparison passes while the broad checkout fails at the same revision.

## Defect legitimacy

`docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the selected SHA. It also defines the full SHA as the code version the gate verifies. Fetching unrelated heads is outside that contract and prevents supported gates from completing. This is a defect.

## Remediation constraints

- Preserve freshness for moving branches and tags.
- Preserve targeted recovery for a full SHA that is absent locally.
- Preserve complete blob acquisition for the selected tree.
- Preserve `--end-of-options` protection for client-supplied refs.
- Do not narrow or rewrite the checkout owner's configured refspec as a side effect.
- Keep attested mode fail-closed when the selected ref or required object cannot be obtained.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A locally resolvable full SHA does not trigger a general fetch whose scope expands through `remote.origin.fetch`.
- [ ] A moving branch or tag is refreshed before resolution.
- [ ] A missing full SHA uses a targeted fetch and either resolves or fails closed with an actionable error.
- [ ] Materialization acquires every missing blob for the selected tree without fetching unrelated heads.
- [ ] A deterministic local-remote test uses a broad refspec and a large unrelated branch, then proves that resolving and materializing a present SHA does not transfer the unrelated objects.
- [ ] Existing snapshot security, partial-clone, timeout, and concurrency tests remain green.
- [ ] Current snapshot documentation describes fetch scope for full SHAs, moving refs, and missing objects.
- [ ] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.
compiled_state.title: Attested exact-SHA snapshot performs a broad no-filter fetch across every origin head
